title: Why it moved (data/market/why.json)
description: Short notes, in our own words and with dated links to allow-listed sources, on why one of our names, a context fund or a sector moved unusually on a market day. Researched by a scheduled Claude session (routine why_notes, never the brain), recorded by .github/workflows/why.yml through scripts/record_why.py, which fills move_pct and symbols from our own data. They explain a move; they are never a reason to trade and never enter the brain's pack. The newest thirty days are kept.

as_of.description: The newest market day with a note.

move_pct.description: The day move in percent, computed by code from our derived data (never by the model).

symbols.description: The names the move covers, from our data: the stock or fund itself (first), funds that moved with it, or a sector's names.

name.description: Who the note is about in words, from our config (the list name, benchmark label or sector), filled by record_why from the candidate (never by the model). Optional: older files have none.

key.description: A stock or fund: its ticker. A sector average of the main list: sector:<GICS sector>, e.g. sector:Communication Services.

market.description: The config/markets.json id where the move was found.

confidence.description: clear: an official or several reputable sources state the cause; likely: reputable outlets link the move to it; unclear: no allow-listed source explains it, and the note says so.
